h1: The 6 Best Printers for High-Volume Printing of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six printers built for heavy monthly page counts, from compact mono lasers to refillable ink tanks, with who each suits.
summary: The Canon imageCLASS MF753Cdw II is the pick for offices that print constantly and need color. The Brother DCP-L2640DW is the sensible choice for text-heavy workloads, and the Epson EcoTank ET-4950 gives the lowest ongoing ink cost for color-heavy shops. The HP Smart Tank 5101 is the compact, cheaper tank option.
intro: Most people shop for a high-volume printer by looking at the sticker price, then discover that the real bill arrives in toner, ink and replaced parts. A machine that costs less up front but burns through cartridges can end up the most expensive thing in the room within a year.

We reviewed six printers that suit heavy monthly page counts and ranked them on paper: engine type, rated speed, paper handling, running-cost design and warranty. Prices are shown as buckets because they move constantly.

products.name: Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II Wireless Duplex Laser Printer
products.verdict: The fastest and sturdiest machine here for offices that never stop printing.
products.description:
The MF753Cdw II is a color laser rated at 35 pages per minute, with an automatic document feeder and fax, copy and scan all built in. It sits in the $200-500 bucket.

It tops this list because speed and duty design matter most when volume is the goal. The Brother HL-L3220CDW is cheaper but rated at 19 ppm, so a long job takes nearly twice as long here.

Buy it if several people share one machine and color is routine. The caveat is size: it is the biggest unit in this ranking, so check your desk or shelf before ordering.
products.idealFor: Busy shared offices that print in color all day.
products.skipIf: You print a few hundred pages a month or have a tight desk.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser
products.verdict: A compact black-and-white workhorse for text-heavy volume.
products.description:
This is a monochrome laser with automatic duplex printing, a copy and scan function, and wireless and mobile printing in a compact body. It lands in the $200-500 bucket.

It ranks below the Canon because it gives up color and speed, but it is simpler and tends to be cheaper per page for plain documents. Against the color Brother below, the mono engine is the better fit when color never comes up.

Choose it for invoices, contracts and reports. The limit is obvious: if a client ever needs a color chart, you will be outsourcing it.
products.idealFor: Text-heavy offices that never need color.
products.skipIf: You print marketing material or charts.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4950 Wireless Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer
products.verdict: Refillable tanks that keep color cheap over thousands of pages.
products.description:
The ET-4950 uses a cartridge-free refillable tank system rated for up to three years of ink, adds an automatic document feeder and a 2.4-inch touchscreen, and prints at 18 ppm. It is in the $200-500 bucket.

It ranks under the lasers because 18 ppm is slow for a big queue, but it beats them on the cost of color. Against the cheaper ET-4800 below, the touchscreen and the longer rated ink supply justify the step up.

It suits color-heavy small offices that print steadily rather than in bursts. Refilling bottles is messier than swapping toner, which some users will dislike.
products.idealFor: Color-heavy shops wanting the lowest running cost.
products.skipIf: You need fast bursts or mostly black text.

products.name: Brother Color Laser Printer HL-L3220CDW
products.verdict: A modest color laser for steady volume without the Canon bulk.
products.description:
The HL-L3220CDW is a color laser at 19 ppm with automatic duplex, a 250-sheet tray and wireless and mobile support. It sits in the $200-500 bucket.

The L3220CDW lands mid-table since the print-only design and slower speed trail the Canon, and it lacks the Canon's feeder. Compared with the mono Brother above, you pay for color capability you may not use daily.

A good match for offices that print color regularly but not in huge runs. The 250-sheet tray means more frequent reloads under heavy use.
products.idealFor: Offices needing regular color without a big machine.
products.skipIf: You also need scanning or a document feeder.

products.name: HP Smart Tank 5101 Wireless All-in-One Refillable Printer
products.verdict: A small tank printer that ships with two years of ink.
products.description:
The Smart Tank 5101 is a refillable ink tank all-in-one that ships with two years of ink and prints, scans and copies over 2.4GHz wireless. It is in the $100-200 bucket.

It ranks below the Epson tanks because it lacks an automatic document feeder, which slows any scan or copy job of multiple pages. Its smaller body is the trade you get in return.

Best for a home office or small team that wants tank economics on a budget. Note it only joins 2.4GHz networks, which can matter in some offices.
products.idealFor: Small offices wanting cheap color on a budget.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4800 Wireless Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer
products.verdict: Older but capable tank printer with Ethernet and fax.
products.description:
The ET-4800 offers the same refillable EcoTank approach with an automatic document feeder, fax, Ethernet, and a scanner and copier. It sits in the $100-200 bucket.

The ET-4800 closes out the list since theET-4950 above is the newer design with a bigger rated ink supply and a touchscreen. This one is the way to save money without leaving the tank format.

It suits offices scaling from moderate to high volume on a tighter budget, especially ones wanting wired Ethernet. The caveat is an older model with fewer conveniences.
products.idealFor: Budget offices wanting wired network printing.
products.skipIf: You want a touchscreen or the longest ink supply.

methodology.description: We used published pages per minute as a rough guide to how fast a large queue clears.

methodology.description: We looked at how each machine delivers ink or toner and what it implies for long-term cost.

methodology.description: We checked duplex, tray size and document feeders for multi-page work.

methodology.title: Warranty and support
methodology.description: We noted listed warranty terms and connectivity options such as Ethernet.

whatMatters.detail: Laser printers fuse toner with heat and shine at fast text output, while tank inkjets spray liquid ink from refillable reservoirs. Lasers win on speed and sharp text; tanks win on cheap color. Check the listing for the words laser or tank before anything else.

Pages per minute tells you how long a stack takes. At 18 ppm, a 500-page job takes about 28 minutes; at 35 ppm it takes about 14. Look for the ppm figure in the spec bullets and remember it is a best-case rating.

The machine price is only the start. Refillable tanks and high-capacity cartridges lower the cost per page, but cheap cartridge printers cost more over time. Look for tank, INKvestment or high-yield wording on the listing.
Automatic duplex halves paper use, and a document feeder lets you copy or scan stacks unattended. Without one, every page is a manual job. Verify ADF and duplex are named in the listing, not assumed.
A longer warranty signals the maker expects the machine to be used hard, and Ethernet keeps a shared printer stable. Look for the warranty length and the word Ethernet in the spec list.

howToChoose.intro: What you print most decides the engine.

rows: Photos and graphics, low ink cost

cards.label: Laser
cards.text: Fast, crisp text and little maintenance. Picks: Canon MF753Cdw II, Brother DCP-L2640DW and Brother HL-L3220CDW.

cards.label: Ink tank
cards.text: Cheapest color per page but slower and messier to refill. Picks: Epson ET-4950, Epson ET-4800 and HP Smart Tank 5101.

howToChoose.note: Default to laser for text and speed, tank for color volume.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A rated speed above 30 ppm, an automatic document feeder and a multi-year warranty.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Canon MF753Cdw II is the only pick that satisfies all three.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Queues back up daily or color jobs are routine. The Canon MF753Cdw II or Epson ET-4950 pay back quickly.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Volume is moderate and you can live without a feeder. The Epson ET-4800 or HP Smart Tank 5101 do the job.

faq.q: Is a laser or ink tank printer better for high volume?
faq.a: Laser wins on speed and plain text, while ink tanks win on the cost of color. Choose by page mix, not just volume.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Judging by the machine price alone. Toner or ink costs dominate over a couple of years, so check how each model delivers consumables.

faq.q: Is the Canon worth it over the Brother color laser?
faq.a: If you print constantly, yes: 35 ppm versus 19 ppm and a feeder save real time. For modest runs the Brother is plenty.

faq.q: How do I set up a shared printer?
faq.a: Use Ethernet if the model has it, such as the Epson ET-4800, and assign a fixed address. Wi-Fi works but can drop under load.

faq.q: How do I maintain a tank printer?
faq.a: Refill with the matching bottles before tanks run dry and print something weekly so nozzles do not clog.

faq.q: Does the HP Smart Tank work on 5GHz Wi-Fi?
faq.a: No. The listing says 2.4GHz only, so check your router before buying.

finalTake: For genuine heavy use the Canon imageCLASS MF753Cdw II is the machine to buy. Text-only shops should take the Brother DCP-L2640DW, and color-heavy shops should look at the Epson EcoTank ET-4950. Match the engine to your page mix and the rest follows.
